subject: science
q: In a shadow play, the puppet is moved closer to the screen. The shadow becomes
explanation: Moving the puppet nearer the screen and away from the lamp reduces the shadow size.

subject: science
q: A person stands 1 m in front of a plane mirror. How far behind the mirror does her image appear to be?
explanation: The image is as far behind the mirror as the object is in front.

crossCheck.note: Option D (1 m behind the mirror) is the image distance; the stem is ambiguous about whether 2 m total distance is meant. Reworded after review to ask for the distance behind the mirror.

subject: science
q: Mention two methods by which unwanted pregnancy can be prevented.
answer: Barrier methods such as a condom; hormonal methods such as oral contraceptive pills; an intrauterine device such as the copper-T; or surgical methods such as vasectomy and tubectomy.
keyPoints: A barrier method such as a condom
A second method: oral pills (hormonal), copper-T (IUD) or surgery
explanation: Contraceptive methods prevent fertilisation or implantation.

crossCheck.note: Pills and copper-T (IUD) are not barrier methods; the answer mislabels them as barrier methods. Corrected after review: only the condom is a barrier method.

subject: science
q: Which of these molecules contains a double bond between its two atoms?
explanation: In O₂, each oxygen atom shares two electron pairs with the other, forming a double bond.

subject: social
topic: Village Economy and People as Resource
q: Name the four factors of production.
answer: The four factors of production are land, labour, physical capital and human capital (knowledge and enterprise).
explanation: All production needs a combination of these factors.

crossCheck.note: Standard CBSE/NCERT factors are land, labour, physical capital and entrepreneurship. The proposed answer puts human capital in place of entrepreneurship and then describes it as enterprise, which mixes two factors. Check against the textbook wording. Reviewed: the answer follows the NCERT Class 9 Economics wording (human capital = knowledge and enterprise); kept.

subject: social
q: What is an endangered species? Name one from India.
answer: An endangered species is one whose numbers have fallen so low that it is at risk of becoming extinct. The Bengal tiger is an example from India.
keyPoints: Numbers very low, at risk of extinction
An example such as the Bengal tiger
explanation: Such species need special protection.

crossCheck.note: The Bengal tiger is correctly listed as endangered, but the one-horned rhinoceros is classed as Vulnerable by IUCN rather than Endangered. Accept only if the textbook uses a looser sense of the word. Fixed after review: the one-horned rhinoceros is IUCN Vulnerable, so it was removed.

subject: social
q: How did the Non-Cooperation Movement spread in the towns?
answer: Middle-class people left government schools and colleges, lawyers gave up legal practice, and councils were boycotted. Foreign cloth was boycotted and burnt, and the use of khadi and Indian goods rose, though the movement slowed as khadi was costlier.
keyPoints: Boycott of schools, courts and councils
Use of khadi and Indian goods
explanation: The movement combined political boycott with economic self-reliance.

crossCheck.note: Mostly accurate (schools, courts and councils boycotted; foreign cloth burnt; khadi promoted), but the causal claim that the movement slowed because khadi was costlier is debatable and not a standard textbook explanation. Check the wording before use. Reviewed: kept, follows NCERT (Nationalism in India) on khadi being costlier.

subject: social
topic: Print Culture and the Modern World
q: What was woodblock printing, and how did it reach Europe?
answer: In woodblock printing, text or images are carved on a wooden block, inked and pressed on paper. It developed in China, and Marco Polo brought the knowledge to Italy after his travels in the late 13th century.
keyPoints: Marco Polo brought it to Italy
explanation: Woodblock printing was the first printing method in Europe.

crossCheck.note: Woodblock printing did develop in China and the story of Marco Polo carrying the knowledge to Italy is in many textbooks, but historians debate whether he was the channel and the claim is a traditional rather than established fact. Better to attribute it cautiously. Reviewed: kept, follows NCERT (Print Culture); historians debate the Marco Polo route.

subject: social
q: Which landform covers the largest share of India’s area, about 43 per cent?
explanation: Plains cover about 43 per cent, mountains about 30 per cent and plateaus about 27 per cent.

crossCheck.note: Plains cover about 43.9 per cent of India's area (plateaus about 27.7 per cent, mountains about 10.7 per cent), so the 43 per cent in the question points to plains, not plateaus. The answer is A (Plains); the question wording should be checked. Reviewed: kept, matches NCERT figures (43/30/27 per cent); the checker also chose A.

subject: social
q: The official language of the Union of India is
explanation: Hindi in Devanagari script is the official language, and English is also used for official purposes.

crossCheck.note: Article 343 makes Hindi in Devanagari script the official language of the Union, but English is also an official language for official purposes under the same article. Option A is incomplete rather than wrong, so the question wording needs checking. Reviewed: kept, Article 343: Hindi in Devanagari, with English continuing; the explanation says so.

subject: social
topic: Print Culture and the Modern World
q: Who brought knowledge of woodblock printing from China to Italy?
explanation: Marco Polo, the Italian traveller, returned from China with knowledge of woodblock printing.

crossCheck.note: Marco Polo is the textbook answer, but the claim that he brought woodblock printing from China to Italy is traditional and disputed by historians; the question presents it as established. Reviewed: kept, follows NCERT (Print Culture); historians debate the Marco Polo route.

explanation: 'भाई' का स्त्रीलिंग 'बहन' है। 'भाभी' भाई की पत्नी को कहते हैं।

subject: hindi
q: 'पक्षी आकाश में उड़ रहा है।' इस वाक्य का बहुवचन रूप कौन-सा है?
options: पक्षी आकाश में उड़ रहा है।

पक्षियाँ आकाश में उड़ रही हैं।
पक्षी आकाश में उड़ रही हैं।

subject: science
topic: Food: Where Does It Come From?
q: Give three examples of foods we get from plants, each from a different plant part, and name the part.
answer: Carrot is a root, spinach is a leaf and mango is a fruit.
keyPoints: Each example correctly matched to its part
explanation: Plants give us food from roots, stems, leaves, flowers, fruits and seeds.

subject: science
q: What is evaporation? Give one use of it.
answer: Evaporation is the change of a liquid into vapour. It is used to get salt from sea water or to dry wet clothes.
explanation: Evaporation leaves dissolved solids behind.

subject: science
q: Name two living and two non-living components of a pond habitat.
answer: Living: fish and water plants. Non-living: water and soil or rocks.
explanation: A habitat has biotic and abiotic parts.

subject: science
q: Name three magnetic and three non-magnetic materials.
answer: Magnetic: iron, nickel, cobalt. Non-magnetic: wood, plastic, rubber.
explanation: Only iron, nickel and cobalt and their alloys are magnetic.

subject: science
q: State two differences between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells.
answer: A prokaryotic cell has no well-defined nucleus (no nuclear membrane) and no membrane-bound organelles, while a eukaryotic cell has a true nucleus and membrane-bound organelles. Prokaryotic cells are generally smaller, for example bacteria.
explanation: The key difference is the presence or absence of a membrane-bound nucleus.

subject: science
q: Define 1 joule of work.
answer: One joule is the work done when a force of 1 newton displaces an object by 1 metre in the direction of the force.

subject: science
q: State any two postulates of Dalton's atomic theory.
answer: All matter is made of very small particles called atoms, which cannot be divided or created or destroyed in a chemical reaction. Atoms of the same element are identical in mass and properties, while atoms of different elements have different masses and properties.
explanation: Later discoveries showed that atoms can be divided into subatomic particles and that isotopes exist.

subject: science
q: Give two examples of Newton's third law in everyday life.
answer: When we walk, we push the ground backward and the ground pushes us forward. When a balloon releases air backward, the air pushes the balloon forward. A rocket and the recoil of a gun are also examples.
explanation: Any two correct examples with the action and reaction identified are acceptable.

subject: science
q: Explain the formation of sodium chloride by transfer of electrons.
answer: A sodium atom loses its one outer electron to become a Na+ ion, and a chlorine atom gains that electron to become a Cl- ion. The oppositely charged ions attract each other and form an ionic bond in NaCl.
keyPoints: Sodium loses one electron to form Na+
Chlorine gains one electron to form Cl-
explanation: Both ions attain a stable noble-gas arrangement.

subject: science
q: State two changes seen in boys and two changes seen in girls at puberty.
answer: In boys, the voice deepens and facial hair (a beard or moustache) grows. In girls, the breasts develop and menstruation begins. In both, hair grows in the armpits and genital area.
explanation: Hormones trigger these changes at puberty.

subject: science
q: Why is nichrome used in heating elements while copper is used for connecting wires?
answer: Nichrome has a high resistivity and a high melting point and does not oxidise easily at high temperatures, so it heats up well. Copper has very low resistivity, so it carries current with little loss of heat.
keyPoints: Nichrome has high resistivity and melting point
explanation: The choice depends on whether heat is wanted or not.

subject: science
q: Why do astronauts in an orbiting satellite feel weightless even though gravity still acts on them?
answer: The astronaut and the satellite are both in free fall around the Earth with the same acceleration, so there is no contact force between them. Gravity provides the centripetal force, and the apparent weight is zero.
keyPoints: Satellite and astronaut fall together with the same acceleration
Gravity is still acting and supplies centripetal force
No normal reaction, so apparent weight is zero
explanation: Weightlessness means zero apparent weight, not zero gravity.

subject: science
q: The C=O bonds in carbon dioxide are polar, yet the CO₂ molecule has zero dipole moment. Explain.
answer: CO₂ is linear, so the two equal C=O bond dipoles point in opposite directions and cancel each other. The molecule as a whole is therefore non-polar.
keyPoints: Bond dipoles cancel, net dipole moment is zero
explanation: Molecular polarity depends on both bond polarity and geometry.

subject: science
q: Why does a person suffering from anaemia feel breathless on mild exertion?
answer: Anaemia means low haemoglobin or too few red cells, so the blood carries less oxygen. During exertion the tissues need more oxygen, so the person must breathe faster and the heart beats faster to compensate, which feels like breathlessness.
keyPoints: Low haemoglobin means reduced oxygen-carrying capacity
Tissues need more oxygen on exertion
Breathing and heart rate rise to compensate
explanation: Oxygen delivery depends on haemoglobin and blood flow.

subject: science
q: A 1000 kg car moving at 20 m/s is stopped by a constant braking force of 4000 N. Find the stopping distance.
answer: KE = ½ × 1000 × 20² = 200000 J. Work done by the brakes F × d must equal this, so d = 200000 / 4000 = 50 m.
explanation: The work-energy theorem links the braking work to the loss of kinetic energy.

subject: science
q: Describe how the placenta allows exchange between mother and foetus even though their bloods do not mix.
answer: The placenta has villi where foetal capillaries lie close to maternal blood spaces separated by thin membranes. Oxygen, nutrients and antibodies diffuse into the foetal blood while carbon dioxide and wastes pass to the mother, with the two blood supplies kept separate.
keyPoints: Thin membrane between foetal and maternal blood
Oxygen and nutrients pass to foetus
Wastes and CO2 pass to mother
explanation: The placenta also secretes hormones such as hCG, oestrogen and progesterone.

subject: science
topic: Current Electricity and Magnetic Effects of Current
q: Distinguish between diamagnetic, paramagnetic and ferromagnetic materials on the basis of their behaviour in an external magnetic field.
answer: Diamagnetic materials are weakly repelled by a magnetic field and have relative permeability slightly below 1. Paramagnetic materials are weakly attracted and are magnetised along the field. Ferromagnetic materials are strongly attracted and can be permanently magnetised.
explanation: Examples are bismuth, aluminium and iron respectively.

subject: science
q: Why does zinc-coated (galvanised) iron resist rusting even when the zinc coating is scratched?
answer: Zinc is more reactive than iron, so in the presence of moisture it is oxidised in preference to iron and acts as a sacrificial anode. The exposed iron acts as the cathode and is protected from corrosion until the zinc is used up.
keyPoints: Zinc is more reactive than iron
explanation: Tin coating, in contrast, only protects while the surface is intact.

subject: science
q: Why are aliphatic amines stronger bases than ammonia in the gas phase?
answer: Alkyl groups release electrons by the +I effect, which increases the electron density on nitrogen. The lone pair is then more available to accept a proton, and the ammonium ion formed is stabilised by the alkyl groups, so alkylamines are stronger bases than ammonia.
explanation: In water, solvation and steric effects change the order among primary, secondary and tertiary amines.

subject: social
q: State any three rights mentioned in the Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen.
answer: The Declaration stated that men have natural rights such as liberty, property, security and resistance to oppression. It also declared equality before the law and freedom of speech and opinion.
explanation: These rights were described as natural and belonging to every man.

subject: social
q: Describe two features of the Indian desert.
answer: The Thar Desert is a dry, sandy plain west of the Aravali hills with sand dunes and very low rainfall. It has scanty vegetation, and the Luni is its only large river.
explanation: Water is scarce, and life depends on special adaptation.

subject: social
q: What do the terms flora and fauna mean?
answer: Flora means the plants of a region or period, and fauna means the animals of that region or period.
explanation: Together they describe the wildlife of a region.

subject: social
q: Why did the framers of the Constitution choose universal adult franchise from the beginning?
answer: Leaders of the national movement believed in equality, so every adult citizen should have a say in government regardless of wealth, caste or sex. Giving the vote to all gave the new democracy a broad base.
explanation: Universal franchise made political equality real.

subject: social
topic: Industrialisation and the Age of Industry
q: Describe the working conditions of early factory workers in Britain.
answer: Workers, including women and children, put in long hours for low wages. Jobs were uncertain, housing in towns was crowded and unsanitary, and there was little protection from accidents.
explanation: Rapid growth of towns outpaced facilities for workers.

subject: social
q: Why is manufacturing called the backbone of economic development?
answer: Manufacturing makes goods from raw materials, adds value and creates jobs, which reduces dependence on agriculture. Manufactured exports bring foreign exchange and industrial growth raises income and living standards.
explanation: Manufacturing supports growth and reduces poverty.

subject: social
topic: Money, Credit, Globalisation and Consumer Rights
q: What can a consumer do on receiving a defective product, and why is consumer awareness important?
answer: A consumer can complain to the seller, and if not satisfied approach the District, State or National consumer commission with proof of purchase. Awareness of rights helps people avoid being cheated and take action.
explanation: Informed consumers can seek redress.

subject: social
q: Why did the framers adopt a federal structure with a strong Centre?
answer: India is a large, diverse country, so power was divided between the Union and the states. After Partition, unity and integrity were a priority, so the Centre was made strong.
keyPoints: Division of powers between Centre and states
explanation: The design balances regional diversity and national unity.

subject: science
q: If the momentum of a body is doubled (its mass staying the same), by what percentage does its kinetic energy increase?
explanation: KE = p²/2m. Doubling p makes KE four times the original, which is an increase of 300%.

explanation: Electric current is one of the seven base quantities; force, energy and pressure are derived.

explanation: TT, Tt, Tt and tt give 3 tall to 1 dwarf; the genotypic ratio is 1:2:1.

subject: science
q: In a rotating-coil AC generator, the induced emf is maximum when the plane of the coil is
options: at 45 degrees to the field only
explanation: When the plane is parallel to the field, the flux is zero but changing at the greatest rate, so the emf is maximum.

subject: science
q: How many ions are produced per formula unit when [Co(NH3)6]Cl3 dissolves in water?
explanation: It gives one [Co(NH3)6]3+ ion and three Cl- ions, four ions in all.

subject: social

q: Which treaty of 1919 imposed harsh terms on Germany after the First World War?
explanation: The Treaty of Versailles took away German territory, limited its army and demanded reparations.

subject: social

explanation: Many people move to cities for work, education and health care.

subject: social

subject: social
q: The Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi and Beas are tributaries of which river system?

subject: social

q: Which institution is the central bank of India?
explanation: The Reserve Bank of India supervises banks and issues currency.

subject: social

q: Why did the Bretton Woods system use fixed exchange rates?
options: To bring stability to currencies and encourage trade by avoiding sharp changes
explanation: Fixed, adjustable rates were meant to avoid the instability that had hurt world trade between the wars.

They are located only in cities
Electricity is not used in smelting
explanation: Smelting aluminium consumes large amounts of electricity.

q: The prashasti on the Allahabad pillar mainly praises which Gupta ruler?
explanation: The inscription, composed by Harishena, glorifies Samudragupta's achievements.
